basis: Metabolic autoinflammation with defining neurodevelopmental impairment; cataracts 3/3. Myopathy, anemia and hepatosplenic involvement omitted at four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental impairment, progressive ataxia and cerebral/cerebellar atrophy define severe mevalonic aciduria; developmental delay reported in 16/16.

basis: Cardiac and brain malformations characterize the syndrome; nervous abnormalities 80-99%. Finger contractures occur in 30-79%; renal anomaly frequency is unestablished.

decisions.neurologic: primary: structural brain malformations are part of the syndrome's definition, supported by nervous-system abnormalities in 80-99%.

basis: Skin/fascial fibrosis and fixed contractures define disease; myopia 6/8 supports ocular dysfunction. Reflux lacks established direct GI injury; neuropathy 2/8 is below threshold.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: fixed joint contractures and restricted mobility are defining manifestations; elbow contractures occurred in 8/8 and knee contractures in 7/8.

basis: Recurrent hypertensive anterior uveitis defines the ocular disorder. CMV-associated cases form a subset; a disease-wide infectious or autoimmune mechanism is not established.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: ocular inflammation alone does not establish infection or immune-mediated disease; CMV association applies to a subset rather than the syndrome universally.

basis: Heart/brain malformations define syndrome; visual impairment and finger contractures each 1/2. Contractures affect locomotor function; cleft lip 1/2 omitted at cap. Small samples.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none at four-axis cap: cleft lip occurs in 1/2, but functionally significant ocular impairment and joint contractures take priority.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: camptodactyly in 1/2 supports structural joint involvement (~50% of assessed patients); confidence limited by the small denominator.

basis: Secondary glaucoma directly damages the ocular optic nerve. The definition includes heterogeneous inflammatory and steroid-related pathways without a universal infectious or autoimmune cause.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: inflammation-associated glaucoma does not itself establish infection or immune-mediated disease; underlying uveitis has heterogeneous causes.

basis: Adrenal cortisol excess causes muscle wasting/bone loss in >50% and skin atrophy/easy bruising in roughly 50-70%. Hypertension is separately diagnosed secondary hypertension.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertension (~70-80%) is a separately diagnosed secondary disease; direct cardiac or vascular injury is not established in at least 30%.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: cortisol directly causes dermal atrophy and capillary fragility with easy bruising in roughly 50-70%; these are intrinsic manifestations.

basis: Bone fragility and congenital contractures define disease. Respiratory insufficiency occurs in 30-79%, but skeletal restriction does not establish direct pulmonary damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: frequent respiratory insufficiency (30-79%) generally reflects thoracic skeletal restriction; the evidence does not establish direct lung or airway disease.

basis: Cryptophthalmos, syndactyly and renal malformations are major criteria; renal defects 80-99%. Laryngeal stenosis/hypoplasia 30-79%; GI and ear anomalies omitted at cap.

decisions.renal: primary: renal agenesis/hypoplasia is a major diagnostic criterion, supported by renal hypoplasia/aplasia and urinary abnormalities in 80-99%.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment defines disease. Dry skin occurs in 6/12 but does not establish tissue injury or functional loss; isolated joint/dental reports lack reliable prevalence.

decisions.dermatologic: none: dry skin in 6/12 meets the frequency threshold but alone does not demonstrate direct tissue damage or functional loss; cutis laxa is an isolated report.
